title: Lemon and Garlic Chicken Traybake
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs roasted over potatoes that soak up the lemony, garlicky juices. One tin, very little washing up.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Tip the potatoes, onions and garlic cloves into your largest roasting tin, add 2 tbsp of the oil and half the salt, and toss. Spread out in one layer and roast to give them a head start.
steps.tip: The tin needs to be big enough that nothing is piled up, or the potatoes will steam and stay pale.

steps.text: Meanwhile, zest one lemon into a bowl. Add the remaining oil, the oregano, the rest of the salt and plenty of pepper, then add the chicken and rub the mixture all over, including under the skin where you can. Juice the zested lemon into the stock. Cut the second lemon into 6 wedges.

Take the tin out of the oven and turn the potatoes. Tuck in the lemon wedges and thyme, then sit the chicken on top, skin-side up. Pour the lemony stock around the chicken rather than over it, so the skin stays dry.
Roast until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest thigh next to the bone. A probe thermometer should read at least 75°C.
steps.tip: If the skin is browning too quickly, move the tin down a shelf rather than covering it, which would soften the skin.

steps.text: Leave to rest in the tin. Squeeze the soft garlic out of its skins and stir it through the potatoes and pan juices along with the juice from a couple of the roasted lemon wedges.
Scatter with the parsley and serve straight from the tin, spooning the juices over everything.

tips: Take the chicken out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking so it roasts evenly.
A green salad or some steamed greens is all this needs alongside.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for about 15 minutes, until the chicken is piping hot throughout.
author: Simmer
